title: Should you own a car in Singapore in 2026?
excerpt: Category A COE hit a record S$133,009 on 9 September. Next bid is 21 September. For most households the honest answer is still no — unless school run and two kids make Grab a second job.

body.text: The 9 September 2026 tender put Category A (cars up to 1,600cc and 130 bhp, or 110 kW) at S$133,009 — an all-time high. Category B was S$135,001. Open (E) S$137,890. Motorcycle (D) S$12,556. Next bidding: Monday 21 September, noon; results Wednesday 23 September, 4pm. If you are waiting for COE to ‘come back down before we buy’, you have been saying that since 2023.
What a car actually costs

items: COE is ten years of permission to own the car, not the car. On a Cat A bid at S$133k you are paying more for the paper than for many of the cars it is attached to.
Then: OMV, excise, GST, registration, ARF. A ‘cheap’ compact is not cheap. Budget S$180k–250k on-the-road for something ordinary, more if you have taste.
Petrol or electricity, parking at the condo (S$150–300/month if it is not bundled), ERP, insurance, servicing. ERP 2.0 is distance-and-time charging, not the old gantry surprise — still not free.
After ten years you revalidate at the Prevailing Quota Premium (PQP). September 2026 PQP: Cat A S$126,208, Cat B S$128,697. That is another six-figure decision, not a formality.

body.title: The test
body.text: If you cannot write a cheque for the COE without calling the bank, you cannot afford the car. Singapore will not finance your lifestyle at these premiums and call it middle class.
When a car still wins

items: Two children at two different international schools, neither on an MRT. The 7.15am school run is why Bukit Timah and the east still buy.
A helper who cannot legally drive your car, and a partner who also works. Time is the scarce thing, not the Grab receipt.
Weekend sports that involve a boot: bikes, a dog, a cooler, East Coast at 6.30am.
You already drive, you will be here five years-plus, and the company is paying. Then it is a benefit, not a hobby.

body.text: When it does not

One adult, CBD job, Tiong Bahru or Tanjong Pagar walk-up: you will spend more on the car than on rent. SimplyGo, a folding bike, and Grab for the wet night is how most of the island actually moves. The adult monthly travel pass is S$122. A mid-range Grab to town is S$18–28. Do the arithmetic for a month before you bid.
If you still want one

items: Lease or company car first. You are renting the depreciation and the COE together. Get the number in writing.
Parallel import vs authorised: warranty and workshop access matter more than the sticker once something breaks.
Do not bid Cat E ‘because it is flexible’ unless you know why. You are paying Open-category money for the privilege of competing with everyone.
Off-peak cars exist. They are a lifestyle with a clock. Fine if your use is weekends; misery if your use is 8am school.

body.title: 21 September
body.text: If you are bidding this round, set a ceiling tonight and do not raise it in the last ten minutes because a group chat got loud. LTA does not care that your child starts term.

title: Your condo is not a country
excerpt: The pool has hours. The BBQ pit is a booking, not a birthright. Renovation is weekdays. Security will call you about the Grab. Learn the house rules in week one or you become the WhatsApp screenshot.

body.text: A Singapore condo is a small town with a gym, a WhatsApp group, and a set of by-laws you did not write. The Management Corporation (MCST) runs the common property. Security works for them, not for your delivery driver’s parking style. You rent a unit. You do not rent the right to treat the function room as your living room.
The rules that actually bite

items: Pool, spa, gym: posted hours. Children in the adult lap lane is how you meet the committee. Towels on sunbeds for three hours while you go to work is how you meet them faster.
BBQ pits and function rooms: book on the condo app or at the management office. Deposit, time slot, clean-up. The pit is not first-come on Saturday at 4pm because you saw it empty.
Renovation: typically weekday daytime only, a deposit, a permit, no hacking on Sundays. Your contractor already knows. You are the one who has to file it. Start two weeks before the sofa arrives.
Visitor parking: coupons or a QR, not ‘I’ll just be five minutes’. The barrier arm does not care that you are late for the school run.

Short-term stays: most MCSTs ban anything that looks like Airbnb. Your lease probably does too. So does the law, for stays under three months in a private residential unit without the right approvals.

body.title: Noise
body.text: Mahjong, a baby, a dog, a Sunday roast — all legal. A 11pm speaker facing the courtyard is how you get a notice. Flooring: many stacks require acoustic underlay before you put down timber. Ask before you ‘refresh’ the unit.
HDB is a different country

If you rented an HDB, there is no MCST. There is a town council, a void deck, a corridor you do not block, and neighbours who have lived there since before your pass existed. Conservancy charges are in the rent. BBQ pits are still booked, just through a different app. Laundry on a stick is normal. Judging it is the fastest way to stay an outsider.
How not to be the unit in 27-04

items: Read the house rules PDF the agent buried in the email. Print the pool hours on the fridge.
Register every person in the household with security, including the helper and the baby. Cards, tags, face ID — whatever this building uses.
Do not hold the carpark barrier with your body for a friend. Do not prop the fire door with a yoga mat.
Drip umbrellas, wet shoes, gym sweat: the lift is shared. A towel costs less than a complaint.
The residents’ WhatsApp is not customer service. Defects go to management. Neighbour disputes go to management, then the Community Mediation Centre, not a thread of 40 people.

body.title: Facilities are why you pay
body.text: You paid for the pool in the rent. Using it at 7am is the point. Using it as a private party for twelve without a booking is how the AGM gets ugly. Be the household that books, cleans, and leaves on time.

title: A gym that is not a 12-month hostage
excerpt: ActiveSG is S$2.50–3.30 a visit or S$15–30 a month. Pure and Fitness First are a different sport. True Fitness shut every club on 10 September. Start at the heartland gym; upgrade only if you actually go.

body.text: Singapore will sell you a gym the week you land. Towels, eucalyptus, an iPad at reception, a 12-month debit. Most people need a rack, a fan, and a shower that works. ActiveSG still exists for that. True Fitness does not: every club closed on 10 September 2026. If you are still paying them, stop and write to the liquidator, not the front desk.
The actual prices, September 2026

items: ActiveSG MyActiveGYM, adult: S$30/month peak, S$15 off-peak (weekdays to 4pm, no public holidays). S$300 for 12 months peak. Per-entry about S$2.50 for citizens/PRs, S$3.30 standard (that is you, on an EP). Swim: S$10/month unlimited for adults. ~30 gyms, heartland, no eucalyptus.
Anytime Fitness: franchise, quoted per club, often S$98–158/month. 160-odd outlets. Fine if you travel and want 6am in Tampines.
Fitness First: around S$200 home-club, S$225 passport across 14 clubs, 4- or 12-month lock-in. FITPASS credits if you refuse a contract.
Virgin Active: weekly plans from about S$41, or S$220–265/month depending on how they package it this quarter. Recovery rooms. Sales desk.
Pure Fitness: two CBD rooms, enquiry-led, published somewhere between S$175 and S$400. Sprint track. Juice. You know if this is you.

body.title: EP holders
body.text: ActiveSG membership is not only for citizens. You pay the standard entry, not the subsidised one. That is still cheaper than a joining fee at a mall gym you will ghost after Chinese New Year.
The condo gym is a trap

Two treadmills, a cable machine with a snapped pin, and a neighbour on a work call. Use it for the week you arrive. Then go to the ActiveSG nearest the MRT you already take. Guillemard, Heartbeat@Bedok, Our Tampines Hub, the one under the HDB — they are the actual network. Peak 7–8.30pm is a queue. Off-peak is the membership that makes sense if you work from home.
How to decide in one lunchtime

items: If you will go twice a week: ActiveSG per-entry. Do not sign anything.
If you will go four times and you live near a decent ActiveSG: S$30 peak or S$300/year.
If the gym is also your social life (classes, the same 7am faces): Anytime or a studio. That is a calendar, not equipment.
If your company is paying: take Virgin or Fitness First and do not pretend it is a personality.
Never prepay 12 months to a chain you have not visited at 7am on a Monday. True Fitness is the 2026 reminder.

body.label: Repeating rooms, if you want people not machines

title: Joo Chiat after eight
excerpt: Not a Peranakan museum with a queue. The east after work: laksa arguments, shophouse bars, Marine Parade for the actual dinner, and the TEL stop that finally made this a Tuesday neighbourhood.

body.text: East Coast Road is the postcard. Joo Chiat Road is where people who live here actually walk after 8pm. The shophouses are still shophouses. The laksa argument is still an argument. Tanjong Katong MRT (TEL) is what changed the neighbourhood from a taxi decision into a Tuesday. If you only came for the colourful facades and left, you did the tourist version.
Laksa, then move

Katong laksa is coconut, cut noodles, a fork. The stretch around East Coast Road / Ceylon Road still has the old names fighting about who is original. Pick one, sit down, do not film the bowl. It is a S$6–8 lunch that people from the east will grade you on. Then leave. The neighbourhood is longer than one soup.

items: Kueh and pastry in the same few blocks in the late afternoon, before they sell out. If you wait until 8pm you get the fluorescent leftovers.

Nasi lemak, banana leaf, and the Marine Parade hawker centres are the weeknight dinner. Joo Chiat Road restaurants are the Friday. Do not spend S$48 on a ‘heritage set’ when the hawker two bus stops away is better.
Cafés on Joo Chiat are for Saturday 10am. After eight they turn into wine and small plates. That is allowed.

body.text: Drink like you live two streets over

The independent bars hide on the side streets and in the shophouses without a PR firm. One cocktail is S$20–28, same as Tanjong Pagar, but you can hear the person opposite. Last train on the TEL is the constraint, not the lock-in. Grab from here to Tiong Bahru is a long, expensive sulk — stay east or go home.

body.title: Parking and rain
body.text: Street parking fills by 7.30 on Friday. The malls on East Coast / Marine Parade are the overflow. Flash floods still pick the same low Katong pockets. If the canal is angry, walk.
How to use it as a resident

items: Live here if you want shophouse grain, the beach five minutes on a bike, and schools that are not all in Bukit Timah. Read the East Coast / Katong neighbourhood note before you sign a lease on a ‘conservation’ walk-up with no lift.
Do not treat Joo Chiat as Chinatown-for-Instagram. People dry laundry, send kids to tuition, and complain about the new café’s exhaust. Be the neighbour.
Sunday morning: East Coast Park is the run. Joo Chiat is the brunch. Marine Parade is the wet market. In that order.

body.label: East Coast / Katong as a place to live

title: Bringing the dog (or don’t)
excerpt: Schedule I is Australia, New Zealand, Ireland and the UK — no quarantine if you do the paperwork. Everyone else is a blood test, an agent at Changi, and maybe ten or thirty days in a crate. The condo still has to say yes.

body.text: The Animal & Veterinary Service (AVS, under NParks) is not a vibe. It is a schedule. Pets move on three lists, a microchip, a licence on PALS, and a landlord clause most people read after they have already paid the crate. Since 1 April 2026 you appoint an AVS-recognised pet agent to clear Changi. You do not wander into CAPQ with a carrier and a smile.
The three schedules

items: Schedule I — Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, United Kingdom. No quarantine and no rabies titre if the conditions are met. Still: import licence, vaccinations, parasite treatment, agent at the airport.

Schedule II — US, Canada, Japan, most of the EU, Hong Kong and a few others. Rabies antibody test (RNATT). If the animal arrives within five days of you and has lived at your address more than six months, no quarantine. Otherwise a minimum ten-day home quarantine (apply on FormSG at least four weeks out) or ten days at the Animal Quarantine Centre on a commercial licence.
Schedule III — everywhere else, including most of Latin America, Africa, much of Asia. RNATT with strict timing, then a mandatory minimum 30 days at AQC. Book the kennel months ahead.

body.title: Specified breeds
body.text: Part 1 specified dogs are not allowed in — not to live, not to visit. Do not assume a mix is fine because the seller said so. AVS will look at the animal, not the Instagram caption.
Can you even keep it here?

HDB (Housing and Development (Animals) Rules 2024): maximum two cats and one dog of an approved small breed per flat. No specified breeds. Fine up to S$4,000. Private condos: maximum three cats or dogs combined, and then you still need the MCST and the lease. ‘Pets allowed’ in the listing often means ‘cats, small dogs, not yours’. Get it in the tenancy before you book the flight.
Once they land

items: Licence every cat and dog on pals.avs.gov.sg. First-time owners complete the Pet Ownership Course first.
Fees (from 1 Sep 2026): sterilised, first three animals — S$15 a year, S$25 for two years, or S$35 one-time for life. Non-sterilised: S$90 a year. 10% off for GIRO/online/AXS. Sterilise.
AQC, if you must: fan S$26/day until 30 Nov 2026, then S$36. Air-con S$35, then S$44 from 1 Dec 2026. Plus S$75 transfer from Changi and S$68 if they vaccinate for rabies on arrival.
Leash in public. Cats under physical control. East Coast and the park connectors are the social life. The void deck is not a dog run.

body.text: The honest fork

A young Labrador from Texas into a Tanjong Pagar walk-up is a two-month project and a five-figure invoice once you add agent, crate, flights, titre, and ten days of someone else’s kennel. A Schedule I cat into a pet-ok condo in the east is a paperwork week. If the animal is old, anxious, or you are on a two-year EP, leaving them with family is not a moral failure. Rehoming in the origin country is kinder than a 30-day AQC stay and a no-pets clause you missed.

body.title: Start here
body.text: avs.nparks.gov.sg for the current veterinary conditions (April 2026). Then the agent. Then the landlord. In that order.

title: Having a baby here: the 2026 version
excerpt: Public wards from about S$1,500. Private packages from about S$10,000 before the extras. Government-paid maternity leave is for citizen children. Read the bill before you pick a gynae because of a friend’s Instagram.

body.text: Singapore is an excellent place to deliver a baby and an expensive place to do it without a plan. The hospital is the easy part. The hard parts are: which ward you are actually allowed into, whether MediSave or your insurer will touch the bill, and whether your leave is the 16-week government scheme or the 12-week Employment Act version. Most expat parents are on the second.
What the bill looks like in 2026

Typical vaginal-delivery bills (MOH-style ranges, not a quote): KKH B2 about S$2,000–2,700; KKH or NUH A-class about S$6,000–7,500; Thomson or Raffles single about S$10,000–15,000; Mount Elizabeth or Gleneagles single about S$12,000–16,000. C-section is roughly 1.5–2×. Private ‘packages’ rarely include NICU, epidural extras, or a long stay. Ask for the exclusion list in writing.

items: KKH still delivers more babies than anywhere else on the island. Public, busy, competent. Subsidised B2/C is for citizens and some PRs — most EP families sit in A/B1 or go private.
NUH if you already live west. SGH if you already live south. Do not pick a hospital an hour from your condo because the lobby is nicer.
Thomson Medical is the classic private maternity hospital. Mount E, Gleneagles, Raffles, Mount Alvernia, Parkway East (halal confinement menu) if you already have a gynae there.
Antenatal private packages often land around S$2,000–5,000 before delivery. That is scans and consults, not the birth.

body.title: Insurance first, gynae second
body.text: Call the insurer the week you see two lines. Maternity is often excluded for 10–12 months, or capped, or only paid if the rider was in force before conception. A Mount E lobby is not a benefits table.
Leave: citizen baby vs everyone else

items: Government-Paid Maternity Leave is 16 weeks, and it is for a Singapore-citizen child plus the usual service rules. Reimbursement ceiling is S$10,000 per four weeks. First two child orders: eight weeks employer, eight government; later orders mostly government.

If the child is not a citizen — the usual EP/S Pass case — you are on the Employment Act: 12 weeks, of which the paid portion depends on service and your contract. Read the contract. Do not assume 16.
Paternity and shared parental leave are also built around citizen children. Your company’s handbook may be more generous than MOM. Get HR to write the dates.

body.text: The baby is a person. ICA needs to know.

Register the birth. Apply for a passport from your embassy (timelines vary; US/UK/AU/EU are not the same week). Then a Dependant’s Pass or Long-Term Visit Pass through MOM, tied to the working parent’s pass. The baby cannot ‘just stay on the tourist stamp’. Schools, polyclinics and travel will all ask. Start the DP while you are still on confinement leave, not the week before you fly to see grandparents.
The unglamorous list

items: Confinement nanny vs helper vs parents flying in. A good confinement nanny is booked months out and is not cheap. A helper is a different legal relationship — see the helper piece.
Paediatrician: polyclinic if you have access; private if you want same-week appointments and English notes for the home-country file.
Vaccinations follow the National Childhood Immunisation Schedule. Keep the booklet. International-school nurses will ask.
If you plan to leave Singapore within a year, say so to the gynae. Discharge summaries and growth charts travel better than WhatsApp photos.

body.title: Public is not a consolation prize
body.text: KKH and NUH A/B1 are where a large number of doctors would send their own. Private is privacy, a known gynae, and a quieter night. Neither choice is a personality.

title: How to walk into a hawker centre without looking lost
excerpt: The first meal that makes you feel like you live here is not at a hotel buffet. It is chicken rice at a round table, tray in hand, uncle already taking the next order.

body.text: If you only eat in Holland Village for the first six months, you will have lived in a very expensive version of home. The city happens at hawker centres. They are not rustic. They are the national canteen — air-conditioned now, in many cases, and still S$4–8 a plate.
The move

items: Walk the whole loop once before you queue. The good stall is rarely the first one you see from the door.
Look at the trays coming off the counter, not the plastic photos. If those plates look like what you want, stand there.
Have your order ready: “chicken rice, steamed, no cucumber, teh peng.” Singapore rewards speed, not speeches.
Pay when the food comes unless they take it first. NETS/PayNow is normal in 2026; keep a S$10 note anyway.
Share a round table. That is not a social invitation. Put your packet of tissues down to hold a seat, then go queue.

body.text: Five centres that teach you the island

items: Maxwell (Chinatown) — tourist-heavy, still the fastest education in chicken rice, and the Tian Tian queue is a Singapore conversation starter.
Old Airport Road — the east-side encyclopedia. Satay, oyster omelette, fried carrot cake. Go hungry.
Tiong Bahru Market (upstairs) — breakfast with the neighbourhood. Downstairs is the wet market; that is the second lesson.
Chomp Chomp (Serangoon Gardens) — night, open-air, the stall you will argue about with colleagues.
Our Tampines Hub / a heartland mall food court — this is how most of the country actually eats on a Tuesday.

body.text: “Tissue packet on the table” is a reservation. Do not move someone else’s. Do not be precious about sitting with strangers.
body.title: The packet

body.text: What to order when you have no idea

Chicken rice. Economic rice (cai png) if you want vegetables and three dishes pointed at with a pair of tongs. Minced meat noodles. Fish soup. Nasi lemak. If it is spicy, say “not too spicy” once — they will still make it Singapore-spicy.
Drink: kopi (coffee with condensed milk), kopi-o (black, sugar), kopi-c (evaporated milk), teh peng (iced tea). “Peng” means iced. You now speak a little of the language of the morning.

title: A weekend that is not Orchard Road
excerpt: The island is 50 km across. You can spend two years shopping the same three malls, or you can learn the coast, the reservoir, and the Causeway.

body.text: Orchard is for when you need a phone fixed or a cinema with reserved seats. It is not a personality. The people who stay sane here have a Saturday loop that does not involve ION.
Saturday morning

items: Parkrun at East Coast or West Coast if you can bear 7.30am humidity. It is free, it is the same people every week, and that is how you make friends without “networking”.
MacRitchie Reservoir — the Treetop Walk if you book, the boardwalk if you do not. Go before 8am or you will melt.
East Coast Park: rent a bike at the McDonald’s end, ride toward Bedok, eat seafood at the chalets, swim if the flag is green.

body.text: Saturday afternoon, when it rains

It will rain. Plan B is a museum with aircon (National Gallery is actually good; the Peranakan Museum is the one you should have gone to already) or a hawker centre you have not done. Do not default to a mall unless the children are melting.
Sunday without leaving the island

items: Southern Ridges: Henderson Waves at golden hour. You will share it with wedding photographers. Still worth it.
Pulau Ubin if you want to remember that Singapore used to be kampung. First-come bicycles at the jetty. Last bumboat is real — check the time.
Kampong Glam in the late afternoon, mosque first, then Haji Lane when the light goes pink, then dinner that is not a burger.

body.text: Car ownership here is a lifestyle choice, not a default. A weekend with EZ-Link/SimplyGo, a folding bike, and Grab for the last kilometre is how most new arrivals actually live.

title: How to belong in 90 days
excerpt: A pass is permission to work. Belonging is a kopi uncle who starts your order when you walk in, a clinic that has your file, and one person who would collect your mail.

body.text: The lonely version of this city is a condo with a pool you never use and a Grab history of the same four restaurants. The other version is smaller, cheaper, and much more Singapore.
Week 1–2: the boring infrastructure of a life

items: Pick a GP within walking distance. Parkway, Raffles, or a neighbourhood clinic — you need a name, not a hospital A&E for a sore throat.
Open the bank account, get PayNow, put your Singpass (if you have an EP/S Pass) to work. Cash is for the one stall that still wants it.
Learn the bus that actually serves your block, not just the MRT. The last mile is where you live.

body.text: Week 3–6: one repeating thing

Join one thing that meets every week. Not a Facebook group. A physical room. Hash House Harriers, a running club, a church, a mosque, a temple, CrossFit if you must, a language class at the community centre, Toastmasters, a football pitch booked on ActiveSG. The content of the hobby matters less than the fact that the same 20 people see you on Thursday.
Week 7–12: get slightly local

items: A hawker stall that knows you. That is not poetry. That is how lunch works.
One Singaporean colleague you could text on a Sunday. You have to go first.
A wet market Saturday. Even if you still buy yoghurt at Cold Storage.
Learn two festival dates that are not Christmas. Show up to one.

body.text: Do not build your entire social life inside the nationality bubble. It is comfortable and it is how people leave after three years still unable to order in a kopitiam.
body.title: The compound

body.text: Belonging here is not becoming Singaporean. It is being a person the city can place. Address, clinic, stall, club, one friend who is not on your payroll. That is the whole trick.

title: Kopi, teh, and the rest of breakfast
excerpt: Singapore breakfast is a dialect. Once you can order it, mornings get cheaper and better.

body.text: A kopitiam is a coffee shop, often with a few cooked-food stalls around a drinks uncle who has been there longer than your visa category has existed.
The drinks

items: Kopi — coffee with condensed milk, the default.
Kopi-o — black, sugar. Kopi-o kosong — black, no sugar.
Kopi-c — evaporated milk, less sweet.
Kopi peng — iced. Siu dai — less sugar. Gah dai — more, if you must.
Teh follows the same grammar. Teh tarik is pulled milk tea.
Yuan yang — coffee plus tea. It is not a joke.

body.text: The plate

Kaya toast (coconut jam, cold butter, grilled bread) and two half-boiled eggs with white pepper and dark soy. That is the national breakfast. Add a plate of nasi lemak if you are actually hungry. It will still be under S$8.
Pointing at the menu like a tourist is fine once. The second time, say the words. Uncles are not waiting to be your language teacher, but they are waiting for you to decide.

title: The 2026 holidays, and what they actually are
excerpt: Singapore does not close for your home country’s calendar. It closes for other people’s holy days — and then the whole island goes somewhere.

body.text: If you treat public holidays as “a day off”, you will spend them in a mall. If you treat them as other people’s festivals, the city opens.
Still ahead in 2026

items: Mid-Autumn Festival — Friday 25 September. Mooncakes in the office, lanterns at the Chinese Garden and in Chinatown. You will be offered a snow-skin. Accept it.
Deepavali — 8 November. Little India is the point. Go in the evening. Eat. Do not complain about crowds you walked into.
Christmas is a shopping season here, not a shutdown. 25 December is a holiday; 26th is often a working day. Plan flights accordingly.

body.text: Already passed, learn them for next year

items: Chinese New Year — the two-day close, reunion dinners, ang bao etiquette if you have children of friends, and the week the CBD is empty.
Hari Raya Puasa / Haji — visit if you are invited. Bring a box of cookies. Remove your shoes.
Vesak — temples, and a quieter kind of crowd.
National Day, 9 August — the parade if you balloted; the heartland fireworks if you did not. Wear red if you want to. Nobody will make you.

body.text: Do not book a moving truck, a helper’s rest-day swap, or a government appointment on the eve of CNY or a long weekend. Half the island is already on the Causeway.

title: After-school, without going broke
excerpt: Enrichment is an arms race. Playgrounds, ActiveSG, libraries and the void deck are still how a lot of this country raises children.

body.text: International-school Saturdays can become a second mortgage of swimming, Mandarin, coding and “social tennis”. Some of that is useful. Most of it is other parents’ anxiety, priced in SGD.
The free and almost-free layer

items: NLS / NLB libraries — air-conditioned, board books, and the only place a toddler can be loud-ish at 4pm without a membership.
Neighbourhood playgrounds and void decks. This is not slumming it. This is Singapore. The children you want your child to meet are already there.
ActiveSG sports centres — public pools and courts. Book on the app. Non-citizens pay more; it is still not a country club.
Gardens by the Bay outdoor gardens are free. The Cloud Forest is the paid bit, and you do not need it every weekend.

body.text: When you do pay

Pick one thing the child actually likes. Swim is the one that matters in a country of condominium pools and sudden rain. Mandarin is the one that pays off if you stay. Everything else can wait until they ask.

The “expat playground” circuit (Botanic Gardens playground, East Coast, Sentosa) is real and pleasant. Alternate with a heartland town square or you will raise a child who thinks Singapore is a park with a food court.

title: PayNow, NETS, and the death of cash
excerpt: By week two you should be able to split a hawker bill, pay a helper, and settle a Grab without opening a wallet.

body.text: Singapore in 2026 is allergic to notes. The stall that only takes cash still exists. It is not the majority, and you will feel it when you are the person holding up the queue counting coins.
What to set up

items: A local bank account (DBS/POSB, OCBC, UOB) linked to PayNow via NRIC or mobile. This is how people send you money.
The bank’s app — DBS PayLah! if you went DBS. Scan QR. That is lunch.
NETS on a debit card for the supermarket and the MRT/bus (SimplyGo).
GrabPay or a credit card for rides. Do not use cash with a Grab driver unless you said so in the app.

body.text: The helper, the landlord, the school
Maids are often paid via PayNow. Landlords still love a bank transfer on the 1st. Schools will give you a GIRO form and look at you until you fill it in. GIRO is the adult version of belonging.
Keep S$20–50 cash for the one taxi with a broken machine, the temple donation, and the uncle who has not joined 2026. That is the whole cash strategy.

title: Resident exits: JB, Bintan, Desaru
excerpt: The island is small. Leaving it is a sport. Do it like someone who has to be at work on Monday.

body.text: Leaving Singapore for 36 hours is how you stay. The mistake is treating it like a holiday to another country. It is a valve.
Johor Bahru

KTM into JB Sentral if you want to skip the Causeway car park. CIQ on a Saturday morning is a personality test. Go for seafood, dental work, a tailor, or a hotel with a pool that costs what a Tanglin lunch costs. Be back before Sunday night or you will join the famous queue.
Bintan / Batam
Ferries from HarbourFront. Bintan is resorts and beaches; Batam is more workaday. Passports, not ICs. Book the return ferry before you care about the hotel.
Desaru
A car or a bus, a coast, and a slower Malaysia. Worth it if you have children who need to run in a straight line.
Long weekends: the Causeway is a parking lot. Either leave Thursday night or do not leave. Watch ICA and Waze like a hawk.
body.title: Eve of holiday

title: Don’t be that expat
excerpt: A short list of ways to live here without becoming the story Singaporeans tell about foreigners.

body.text: Singapore is polite until it is not. Most of the rules are not written. Breaking them does not get you deported. It just means people stop explaining things to you.

items: Do not skip the queue. There is always a queue. Join it.
Take off your shoes in homes without being asked.
Do not touch people’s heads. Do not point with your foot.
Speak more quietly on the MRT than you think you need to. Phone speaker in a carriage is a moral failing.
Chewing gum is not a personality. The ban is real enough.
Do not compare everything to “back home” in the first twenty minutes of dinner.
Race and religion are not ice-breakers. CMIO is how the state counts people; it is not your anecdote.
Tip as the card machine suggests, or not at all in hawker centres. Do not perform American tipping in a chicken-rice stall.
Your helper is a worker, not a character in your content.
National Service is not a debate topic you were invited to.

body.text: The positive version: learn names, eat the food, show up to the office lunch, say “sorry ah” when you bump someone, and mean it. That is 90% of looking like you live here.

title: Sports clubs and other repeating rooms
excerpt: Friends in Singapore are a scheduling problem. Book a court, join a hash, or stand on a start line every Saturday.

body.text: People here work late and leave the country on Friday. If your social plan is “we should grab a drink sometime”, you will be alone. If your social plan is a booking, you will see the same faces.
Where repeating happens

items: Hash House Harriers — several hashes, several personalities, beer optional-not-really, jungle optional.
Parkrun — East Coast, West Coast, Bedok, etc. 5 km, Saturday, free.
ActiveSG — book badminton, tennis, football. Non-members of anything can still play.
The traditional clubs (Tanglin, SCC, Dutch, American, British) — expensive, useful if your company pays, not required to have a life.
Climbing gyms, CrossFit boxes, yoga that is not a personality cult. Six months of showing up beats a mixer.
Volunteer: Habitat, animal shelters, migrant-worker groups. Singapore will take your time.

body.text: InterNations and the Facebook groups are how you find the first event. They are not a community. The second event is the one you should go to.

title: F1 month, if you live here
excerpt: The Singapore Grand Prix is 9–11 October 2026 — first Sprint weekend, The Killers, Lana Del Rey. Also: road closures from 7 October. Plan like a resident, not a spectator.

body.text: If you do not have a ticket, F1 is still your problem. LTA closes Marina Centre and Padang-area roads from 12.01am on 7 October through the morning of 13 October. The race itself is 9–11 October under the lights. Last trains from City Hall run late on event nights.
If you are going

items: This is Singapore’s first F1 Sprint weekend. Friday is not a quiet practice day.
Concert stages are bundled with race tickets. The Killers Saturday, Lana Del Rey Sunday — treat that as the reason half your office is “working from home” adjacent to the bay.
MRT. Not a car. Not a Grab that will be surging and stuck.

body.text: If you are not going
Avoid the bay. Eat in the heartlands. Book nothing that assumes you can cross Marina Centre. Host the people who flew in, or leave for JB on Thursday 8 October before the island performs itself.
Work from home those three days if you can. The CBD is a concert with a racetrack in it.

title: Wet market vs Cold Storage
excerpt: You can grocery-shop this island like a hotel guest, or you can learn the morning market and cut the bill in half.

body.text: Cold Storage and Little Farms are where the country stores imported cheese. NTUC FairPrice is where the country actually shops. The wet market is where the fish still has eyes.

items: Wet market (often under a hawker centre): veg, tofu, fish, chicken, cut fruit. Morning. Bring bags. Point, then PayNow.
NTUC — house brands, diapers, the weekly shop. Every town.
Cold Storage / Market Place — when you need the thing from home. You will pay for the feeling.
Mustafa (Little India) — 24 hours, everything, a little chaotic, occasionally the only place that has your home-brand chilli sauce.

body.text: A reasonable split: wet market twice a week for produce, NTUC for bulk, Cold Storage as a treat. Your helper, if you have one, already knows this. Ask her. Pay her for the knowledge.

title: Haze, humidity, and the NEA text
excerpt: The weather here is a policy area. Learn the PSI the way you learned to check rain at home.

body.text: It is hot. It will not stop being hot. The indoor world is 23°C and the outdoor world is a wet towel. You dress for the five minutes between them, which is why people carry a cardigan and still shine.
Haze

When Sumatra burns, Singapore gets a number. PSI. Under 100, live your life. 100–200, kids and the elderly stay in. Above that, the country talks about it on the news and you cancel the East Coast ride. NEA will tell you. So will every group chat.
Rain

Flash floods happen on the same five roads every year. If you live in a low-lying pocket (some of Katong, some of the west), you will learn which. Do not drive into a underpass because the car in front did.
Aircon is not a luxury; it is how paint survives. Budget the bill. A 3-bed on full blast in May is a different number from July in Europe.

title: Mid-Autumn, for people with an office
excerpt: 25 September 2026. Someone will give you a box of mooncakes. Here is what to do with it.

body.text: Mid-Autumn is lanterns and a pastry that is denser than it looks. In an office it is a round of gift boxes: lotus seed, salted egg yolk, the expensive hotel ones, the snow-skin ones from a bakery trying harder.

items: If you receive a box, say thank you and leave it in the pantry unless it has your name on it.
If you give a box, one good one beats four mediocre ones. Do not make it a competition with the other manager.
Take children to a lantern display once. Chinatown or the Chinese Garden. Buy them a paper lantern that will not survive the MRT.

body.text: You do not need to understand the poetry. You need to not walk past the pantry box like it is strange. It is September in Singapore. Eat the cake.

title: After 7pm, where does the city go?
excerpt: CBD empties. Heartlands cook. A few streets get loud. Knowing which is which is the difference between a night out and a deserted pavement.

body.text: Singapore does not have a 2am culture in most postcodes. It has pockets. Standing on a Monday in Raffles Place at 8.30pm wondering where the people went is a rite of passage.

items: Weeknight dinner: Tiong Bahru, Joo Chiat, Ann Siang, Keong Saik, Dempsey if someone else is paying.
Drinks: Duxton, Club Street, Keong Saik, Boat Quay if you like that sort of thing, Tanjong Pagar for the offices that still go out.
Holland Village is a habit, not a discovery. It still works.
Late food: 24-hour kopitiams, prata, and the few hawker centres that run late (not as many as you were promised).

body.text: If you want a city that walks at midnight, you will be disappointed. If you want a city that lets you be in bed at 10.30 and still have had a good evening, you are in the right place.

title: The helper, if you have one
excerpt: A transfer maid is not a subscription. The law is specific. The relationship is the thing that will make or break your household.

body.text: Many expat households here employ a live-in migrant domestic worker. MOM has rules: rest days, levy, medical, insurance, no illegal deployment. Read them. Then behave like a decent employer on top of the rules.

items: A weekly rest day is not a favour. If she works it, pay the extra, in writing.
Food, a bed that is a bed, and a door that closes.
Her phone is hers. Her passport should not live in your safe “for safekeeping” unless she asked.
You are not her parent. You are her boss, in her home, which is also yours. That is a strange arrangement. Stay strange in the direction of respect.

body.text: Budget: salary often S$850–1,200 plus levy (S$300 for many households, concessions exist), plus food and medical. The cheap helper is usually expensive in other ways.
If you do not want a helper, you can live here without one. Plenty of people do. Do not hire someone because the condo WhatsApp assumes you will.
